newsitem.title: UK: Chartwell in bid talks for Archer [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT].
newsitem.headline: Chartwell in bid talks for Archer [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT].

text.p: British underwriting and insurance services company Archer Group Plc said on Friday it was in preliminary bid talks with U.S-based (corrects from Canadian-based) insurance company Chartwell Re Corp, which could lead to a takeover of the UK firm.

Chartwell, which has three wholly-owned subsidiaries called Chartwell Reinsurance Company, The Insurance Corporation of New York and Chartwell Advisers Limited, was likely to make a cash bid with a loan note alternative, Archer said in a statement.
Chartwell may also provide fresh corporate capital to the Archer syndicates under management, it added.
"The making of an offer for Archer would be conditional on, among other things, agreement on terms and conditions and finalisation of due diligence by Chartwell," it stated.
Archers' shares jumped 15 pence to a new year high of 76.5p, valuing the company in market terms at around 28 million stg.
Archer is one of the largest managing agencies in the Lloyd's insurance marketplace with about four percent of Lloyd's total underwriting capacity for 1996.
Any bid is also conditional on Lloyd's insurance market and other required regulatory approvals, it added.
"We are looking forward to joining the Chartwell group who we believe will assist the next stage of development of Archer's business," said Archer's chairman Bryan Kellett.
Chartwell was actively involved in the formation of a Lloyd's listed Corporate Capital Vehicle (CCV) in 1993.

Chartwell Advisers Limited, a licensed Lloyd's adviser and wholly-owned subsidiary of Chartwell, was formed in late 1993 to advise New London Capital Plc NLC.L, which was one of Lloyd's first CCVs publicly traded on the London Stock Exchange.
"This transaction would be a logical and natural extension of our existing activities in the London marketplace," said Chartwell chairman and chief executive Richard Cole.
